# Search Checkpoints

Use `entire search` to find relevant checkpoints before guessing from memory.

## When to Use

- The user asks things like "have we done this before?", "search past work", "find the previous implementation", or "look for checkpoints about X"

## Process

1. Run a focused search with JSON output so results are easy to inspect:

```bash
entire search "<query>" --json
```

Add filters when the user already gave them or when the first search is too broad:

```bash
entire search "<query>" --json --repo owner/name --branch branch-name --author "Name" --date week
```

Inline filters are also supported in the query: `author:<name>`, `date:<week|month>`, `branch:<name>`, `repo:<owner/name>`, `repo:*`.

```bash
entire explain --checkpoint <checkpoint-id> --full --no-pager
```

If `--full` fails, fall back to:

```bash
entire explain --checkpoint <checkpoint-id> --raw-transcript --no-pager
```

## Search Heuristics

- Prefer narrower searches before increasing `--limit`
- Add `--repo` or `repo:*` explicitly when repository scope matters

**How attribution works when a session spans repos.** A session can hold multiple bindings. The first time activity lands in repo B, entire (in global mode) lazily enables B invisibly and writes session state for the *same session ID* into B's `.git/entire-sessions/` — this is essentially the `session adopt` mechanism made automatic. That's the key move for correct attribution: **commit-time linking stays completely local and unchanged.** When the agent commits in repo B, B's own `prepare-commit-msg` hook looks in B's own `.git/entire-sessions/`, finds the session, adds the trailer. No hook ever has to reach across repos at commit time — we moved the state to where the commit will happen, ahead of time, instead of teaching hooks to search other repos.
Per-repo checkpoints then contain that repo's diff plus the shared transcript, and each repo's checkpoint references the same session ID — so from either repo (and from the registry) you can see "this session played out across api/ and web/." That's also exactly what makes the cross-repo read side coherent later: the session, not the repo, is the unit of context.
**Session identity needs a home outside any repo.** A session launched from `~/dev/acme/` has no `.git` to store state in — today that's precisely why it dies. Layer 2 adds a machine-level session record under the userdirs tree (session ID → agent type, transcript path, bound repos). Sessions launched *inside* a repo keep working exactly as today, with the machine record as a thin pointer.
**Binding = automatic adopt.** First time path evidence lands in repo R: if R is enabled (or global mode lazily enables it — Layer 1's job), write session state for the same session ID into R's `.git/entire-sessions/` — reusing the existing `session adopt` machinery, which already handles target-local checkpoint bookkeeping. - Active branch commits: **NO modifications** (no commits created by Entire)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end manual test of global tracking (user-global settings tier).
# Everything runs in an isolated HOME / config / cache so the developer's real
# entire setup is never touched.
set -u

S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BIN="$S/entire-bin"
T="$S/gt"                       # test root
rm -rf "$T"; mkdir -p "$T"
export HOME="$T/home"
export ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$T/config"
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$T/cache"
export ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file
export ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH="$T/tokens.json"
export ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE="$T/auth.json"
export ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1
export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0    # agent sentinel → non-interactive prompts
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$T/gitconfig"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude" "$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR"
echo '{}' > "$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.name "Test User"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.email "test@example.com"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" commit.gpgsign false
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" init.defaultBranch main

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  ✓ $1"; }
bad()  { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  ✗ $1"; }
check(){ if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1"; fi; }
section(){ echo; echo "=== $1"; }
USER_SETTINGS="$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json"
CLAUDE_USER="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"

# --- repo + remote ---------------------------------------------------------
REMOTE="$T/remote.git"; REPO="$T/repo"
git init -q --bare "$REMOTE"
git init -q "$REPO"; cd "$REPO"
git remote add origin "$REMOTE"
echo "# test" > README.md; git add README.md; git commit -q -m "init"; git push -q -u origin main

SID=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
TDIR="$T/claude-project"; mkdir -p "$TDIR"
hook() { # hook <name> <json>
  echo "$2" | ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$TDIR" "$BIN" hooks claude-code "$1"
}
write_transcript() {
  local ts; ts=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
  cat > "$TDIR/transcript.jsonl" <<EOF
{"type":"user","uuid":"$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')","sessionId":"$SID","timestamp":"$ts","message":{"role":"user","content":"$1"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')","sessionId":"$SID","timestamp":"$ts","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done."}]}}
EOF
}
turn() { # turn <file> <content> <prompt>
  hook user-prompt-submit "{\"session_id\":\"$SID\",\"cwd\":\"$REPO\"}" >/dev/null 2>"$T/ups.err"
  echo "$2" > "$1"
  write_transcript "$3"
  hook stop "{\"session_id\":\"$SID\",\"cwd\":\"$REPO\",\"transcript_path\":\"$TDIR/transcript.jsonl\"}" >/dev/null 2>"$T/stop.err"
}

# --- P1: tier unconfigured -------------------------------------------------
section "P1 baseline: no user settings, repo not enabled"
"$BIN" status > "$T/p1.status" 2>&1
check "status says not enabled"            "grep -qiE 'not enabled|disabled|entire enable' $T/p1.status"
turn app.js "console.log(1)" "first prompt"
check "no session state created"           "! ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json"
check "no shadow branch"                   "! git branch --list 'entire/*' | grep -q ."
check "no entire hooks in ~/.claude"       "! grep -q entire $CLAUDE_USER"
rm -f app.js

# --- P2: turn the tier on --------------------------------------------------
section "P2 global.enabled=true"
echo '{"global":{"enabled":true}}' > "$USER_SETTINGS"
"$BIN" status > "$T/p2.status" 2>&1; cat "$T/p2.status" | sed 's/^/    | /'
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p2.json" 2>/dev/null
check "status --json global_tracking.enabled=true"      "jq -e '.global_tracking.enabled==true' $T/p2.json"
check "status --json active_here=true"                  "jq -e '.global_tracking.active_here==true' $T/p2.json"
check "status --json activation_source=global"          "jq -e '.global_tracking.activation_source==\"global\"' $T/p2.json"
check "status --json trust_state reported"              "jq -e '.global_tracking.trust_state|length>0' $T/p2.json"
check "user-level Claude hooks installed"               "grep -q 'entire hooks claude-code' $CLAUDE_USER"
check "worktree still clean (no .entire/)"              "test -z \"\$(git status --porcelain)\""
echo "    trust_state=$(jq -r .global_tracking.trust_state "$T/p2.json") settings_path=$(jq -r .global_tracking.settings_path "$T/p2.json")"

# --- P3: a captured session ------------------------------------------------
section "P3 simulated Claude Code turn in a globally tracked repo"
turn app.js "console.log('hello')" "add hello"
[ -s "$T/stop.err" ] && sed 's/^/    stop stderr| /' "$T/stop.err"
check "git status --porcelain clean (only app.js untracked)" "test \"\$(git status --porcelain)\" = '?? app.js'"
check "no .entire/ in worktree"            "! test -e .entire"
check "runtime root under git dir"         "ls -d .git/entire/worktree/*/metadata"
check "session state written"              "ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json"
check "git hooks lazily installed"         "grep -l entire .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg .git/hooks/post-commit .git/hooks/pre-push"
check "shadow branch exists"               "git branch --list 'entire/*' | grep -q ."
"$BIN" checkpoint list --pending > "$T/p3.pending" 2>&1
check "pending checkpoint listed"          "grep -qiE '[0-9A-Z]{26}|checkpoint' $T/p3.pending"
echo "    runtime root: $(ls -d .git/entire/worktree/*/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

# --- P4: commit → trailer + condensation -----------------------------------
section "P4 commit condenses checkpoint"
git add app.js; git commit -q -m "add hello" 2>"$T/commit.err"; [ -s "$T/commit.err" ] && sed 's/^/    commit stderr| /' "$T/commit.err"
check "Entire-Checkpoint trailer on commit" "git log -1 --format=%B | grep -q '^Entire-Checkpoint: '"
check "entire/checkpoints/v1 exists"        "git rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1"
CP=$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)' | tr -d ' ')
echo "    checkpoint: $CP"

# --- P5: push while untrusted → held ---------------------------------------
section "P5 push without trust holds checkpoint egress"
git push -q origin main 2>"$T/push1.err"; RC=$?; sed 's/^/    push stderr| /' "$T/push1.err"
check "user's push succeeded"              "test $RC -eq 0 && git ls-remote --heads $REMOTE main | grep -q ."
check "stderr explains the hold"           "grep -qiE 'trust|held|not pushed|kept local' $T/push1.err"
check "checkpoints NOT on remote"          "! git ls-remote $REMOTE | grep -q 'entire/checkpoints'"
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p5.json" 2>/dev/null
echo "    trust_state=$(jq -r .global_tracking.trust_state "$T/p5.json") held=$(jq -r '.global_tracking.held_checkpoints // "n/a"' "$T/p5.json")"
check "status reports held checkpoints"   "jq -e '(.global_tracking.held_checkpoints // 0) > 0' $T/p5.json"

# --- P6: trust → next push drains ------------------------------------------
section "P6 entire trust, then push drains the backlog"
"$BIN" trust 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    trust| /'
cat "$USER_SETTINGS" | sed 's/^/    settings| /'
check "trusted_origins recorded"           "jq -e '.global.trusted_origins|length>0' $USER_SETTINGS"
echo "more" >> app.js; git commit -q -am "more" 2>/dev/null
git push -q origin main 2>"$T/push2.err"; sed 's/^/    push stderr| /' "$T/push2.err"
check "checkpoints now on remote"          "git ls-remote $REMOTE | grep -q 'entire/checkpoints'"
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p6.json" 2>/dev/null
echo "    trust_state=$(jq -r .global_tracking.trust_state "$T/p6.json") held=$(jq -r '.global_tracking.held_checkpoints // 0' "$T/p6.json")"
check "trust --revoke removes it"          "$BIN trust --revoke >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! jq -e '.global.trusted_origins|length>0' $USER_SETTINGS"
"$BIN" trust >/dev/null 2>&1

# --- P7: disable in a globally tracked repo writes nothing -----------------
section "P7 entire disable in a globally tracked repo"
"$BIN" disable 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    disable| /'
check "no .entire written by disable"      "! test -e .entire"
check "worktree still clean"               "test -z \"\$(git status --porcelain)\""
check "still active (disable is a no-op)"  "$BIN status --json | jq -e '.global_tracking.active_here==true'"

# --- P8: exclude_paths ------------------------------------------------------
section "P8 exclude_paths deactivates this repo"
jq --arg p "$REPO" '.global.exclude_paths=[$p]' "$USER_SETTINGS" > "$T/tmp.json" && mv "$T/tmp.json" "$USER_SETTINGS"
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p8.json" 2>/dev/null
check "active_here=false"                  "jq -e '.global_tracking.active_here==false' $T/p8.json"
echo "    inactive_reason=$(jq -r '.global_tracking.inactive_reason // ""' "$T/p8.json")"
N0=$(ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json | wc -l)
SID=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'); turn b.js "x" "excluded turn"
check "excluded repo captures nothing"     "test \$(ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json | wc -l) -eq $N0"
rm -f b.js
jq 'del(.global.exclude_paths)' "$USER_SETTINGS" > "$T/tmp.json" && mv "$T/tmp.json" "$USER_SETTINGS"

# --- P9: malformed user settings fail closed --------------------------------
section "P9 unknown key in user settings → tier off, doctor reports"
cp "$USER_SETTINGS" "$T/good.json"
echo '{"global":{"enabled":true,"bogus":1}}' > "$USER_SETTINGS"
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p9.json" 2>"$T/p9.err"
check "tier not active with malformed file" "! jq -e '.global_tracking.active_here==true' $T/p9.json"
"$BIN" doctor > "$T/p9.doctor" 2>&1
check "doctor mentions the user settings problem" "grep -qiE 'settings|global' $T/p9.doctor"
grep -iE 'global|user settings|unknown' "$T/p9.doctor" | head -5 | sed 's/^/    doctor| /'
cp "$T/good.json" "$USER_SETTINGS"

# --- P10: explicit enable switches to local layout -------------------------
section "P10 entire enable in a globally tracked repo → local activation"
"$BIN" enable --agent claude-code 2>&1 | tail -5 | sed 's/^/    enable| /'
check ".entire/settings.json written"      "test -f .entire/settings.json"
"$BIN" status --json > "$T/p10.json" 2>/dev/null
check "activation_source=local"            "jq -e '.global_tracking.activation_source==\"local\"' $T/p10.json"
check "trust recorded by enable"           "jq -e '.global.trusted_origins|length>0' $USER_SETTINGS"
SID=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'); turn c.js "y" "local turn"
check "metadata now in worktree .entire/"  "ls -d .entire/metadata/*"

# --- P11: global.enabled=false removes user hooks --------------------------
section "P11 global.enabled=false → user-level hooks removed"
jq '.global.enabled=false' "$USER_SETTINGS" > "$T/tmp.json" && mv "$T/tmp.json" "$USER_SETTINGS"
"$BIN" status >/dev/null 2>&1
check "entire hooks removed from ~/.claude" "! grep -q 'entire hooks claude-code' $CLAUDE_USER"
check "repo-enabled repo still active"      "$BIN status --json | jq -e '.global_tracking.activation_source==\"local\"'"

echo; echo "==================== $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ===================="
echo "test root: $T"

As of 2026-08-26, `~/Documents` is the iCloud Drive Documents folder
(`~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Documents -> ~/Documents`) and
iCloud "Optimize Mac Storage" is on (`defaults read com.apple.bird optimize-storage` = 1,
~64 GB free). The whole dev tree sits under
`~/Documents/Documents - Peyton’s MacBook Pro/entire/devenv/…` (path has spaces and a
curly apostrophe; it was `~/Documents/entire/devenv/…` before ~Aug 21–24 2026).

Measured 2026-08-26 in entireio/cli: 12,261 evicted ("dataless") files in the main
checkout, 1,053 of them inside `.git/` (`entire-shadow-locks`, `entire-session-locks`,
`entire-sessions`, `hooks`); 83,343 evicted files across 30 of 44 worktrees. Reading one
evicted file blocked 39 s then failed with `Operation canceled`.

**Why:** Any `entire` hook or git command that opens an evicted file blocks on an iCloud
download → Claude Code's 30 s `UserPromptSubmit` default fires ("hook timed out after
30s — output discarded"). Freshly created worktrees (e.g. `claude-hooks` on 2026-08-26)
have 0 evicted files and are fast; older ones stall. Same mechanism behind the
`git fetch`/`git worktree list` hangs noted in [[subagent-display-work]].

**How to apply:** Don't blame the CLI for hook timeouts/hangs in this environment
before checking eviction: `find <dir> -type f -flags +dataless | wc -l`. Never run
broad `grep -r`/`find -exec cat` across old worktrees (each evicted file costs up to
40 s) — read via `git show <sha>:path` instead. Re-hydrate with `brctl download <path>`
as a stopgap. Real fix is user-owned: move the dev tree out of `~/Documents` (or use a
`.nosync` suffix / turn off Desktop & Documents sync or Optimize Storage). Prior
timeout diagnosis (stale `scripts/entire-dev` hook config in old worktrees, fixed by
`a9a676e79`) was a separate, now mostly-resolved cause.

**Migration status (2026-08-26 pm):** `~/migrate-dev-out-of-icloud.sh` moves the tree to
`~/dev/entire`. It first failed because macOS ships `openrsync` (no `-A`/`-X`/
`--info=progress2`); fixed to use `/usr/bin/rsync -aH --partial --progress` (or Homebrew
rsync with full flags if `/opt/homebrew/bin/rsync` exists), and it now also copies
`~/.claude/projects/<old-key>*` → `-Users-peytonmontei-dev-entire*` so history/memory
follow. Not yet run to completion as of this note — if the tree is at `~/dev/entire`,
the iCloud caveats above no longer apply. Separate fix the same day: the repo's
`.claude/settings.json` SessionStart hook had an unquoted `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`
(→ `bash: /Users/peytonmontei/Documents/Documents: No such file or directory`); now quoted.
`bird` (37% CPU, 5 days) and `ApplicationsStorageExtension` (35%) were the CPU hogs — both
iCloud sync/Optimize Storage churning over the 46 GB dev tree.

**Outcome (2026-08-26 evening):** iCloud could not materialize the tree — after the
node_modules/orphan deletions, `bird` had 1.4M sync-up ops queued and 0 drain over 53 min,
downloads sat behind them. Migration by rsync/Download-Now was abandoned. Instead the repos
were **re-cloned from GitHub into `~/dev/entire/devenv/entireio/{cli,docs,entire-api,
entire.io,entiredb,mirror-pipeline}`** (7.4 GB; `entirehq/*` org for entire-api/entire.io/
entiredb/mirror-pipeline, `entireio/*` for cli/docs). cli's push URL is
`entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/entireio/cli`; its uncommitted files, local settings and
`.git/entire-sessions` were copied over; Claude project history copied to key
`-Users-peytonmontei-dev-entire-devenv-entireio-cli`. Work from `~/dev/...` from now on; the
old iCloud tree is pending removal via iCloud Drive off ("Remove from Mac") + server-side
delete at icloud.com. Also cleared that day: go build/mod caches, pnpm/npm caches, Docker
images (named volumes `entire-api-pgdata`/`supabase_db_api` kept), stale mise versions,
$TMPDIR go-build dirs — free disk 67 → 137 GB.

**Follow-up (2026-08-26, later session, still launched from the old iCloud
`.worktrees/antigravity`):** `brctl download` on all 2,719 evicted files hydrated
**zero** of them and `cat` of one evicted file hung >2 min (not 39 s) — iCloud downloads
were fully stalled. `git fetch`, `rev-parse`, `log`, `merge-tree` all worked (no evicted

--hard` (unlink+write, no content reads) is viable to land a new commit in an evicted

## Global-enable user-flow test: 45/48 checks pass

Ran the whole user journey against a dev build in a fully isolated sandbox (own `HOME`, `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, cache, token store, git config; fresh repo + bare remote). Script: `scratchpad/global-test.sh`.

**What a user actually experiences, step by step:**

| Step | What the user does | What they see / what happened | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nothing configured, un-enabled repo, Claude turn | Nothing captured, no hooks anywhere | ✅ |
| 2 | Write `{"global":{"enabled":true}}` to `~/.config/entire/settings.json`, run `entire status` | One-time warning banner; `entire: installed user-level claude-code hooks` (+ gemini); status shows `global tracking: on`, `sync held — repo not trusted · run entire trust`; worktree stays byte-clean | ✅ |
| 3 | Claude turn in the untouched repo | `git status` shows only their file; runtime data lands in `.git/entire/worktree/<hash>/`; git hooks lazily installed; shadow branch + pending checkpoint | ✅ |
| 4 | `git commit` | `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, `entire/checkpoints/v1` condensed | ✅ |
| 5 | `git push` (untrusted) | Push succeeds; stderr: *"checkpoint sync held — this repo isn't trusted yet… run `entire trust`"*; nothing on remote; `status --json held_checkpoints: 2` | ✅ |
| 6 | `entire trust` (GitHub-shaped origin) / `--revoke` | `✓ Trusted github.com/acme/widgets (all clones on this machine)`; revoke re-holds with clear copy | ✅ |
| 7 | `entire disable` in a globally tracked repo | *"Nothing was written."* + exact `exclude_paths` instruction | ✅ |
| 8 | Add repo to `exclude_paths` | `active_here=false`, `inactive_reason=repo_excluded`, turns capture nothing | ✅ |
| 9 | Typo an unknown key in the user file | Tier off machine-wide; `entire doctor`: `USER SETTINGS UNREADABLE … unknown field "bogus"` with fix text | ✅ |
| 10 | `entire enable` in a globally tracked repo | Switches to local `.entire/` layout, `✓ Trusted … for checkpoint sync` recorded automatically | ✅ |
| 11 | Set `enabled: false` | User-level hooks removed on the next command; repo-enabled repo keeps working | ✅ |

**The 3 failures are one finding — a repo whose `origin` is a local path can never sync:**
- `entire trust` → `recording trust: resolving trust identity: configured origin cannot be normalized` (no guidance).
- `entire enable` can't record trust for it either.
- **`trust_all: true` (the push prompt's "Always" answer) does not unlock it** — `DecideEgress` resolves identity before checking `trust_all` and fails closed (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/trust.go:62`). This is deliberate and pinned by `TestEgressDecision_UnparseableConfiguredOriginHolds`, but "Always — trust every repo" then silently excludes local mirrors / bare-path remotes, and the error text doesn't tell the user why or what to do. Worth a decision: honor `trust_all` there, or at least make the message actionable.

**Minor UX notes:** the very first `entire status` after enabling prints `global tracking: on (0 agents covered)` because hook install happens in post-run — the next command shows 2. The banner also fires again whenever the enabled "generation" flips (`trust_all` on↔off) — by design.

**Environment gotchas I hit (saved to memory):** `go build` hung 15+ min because `-buildvcs=auto` runs `git status`, which stalls on this iCloud tree — use `-buildvcs=false`. And your machine already has global tracking on (`~/.config/entire/settings.json` since Aug 12, user hooks since yesterday), so anything you run for real is already in global mode.

## Why a local-path origin can't be trusted

It's a regression of the original design, not an intentional product rule.

- **Aug 17 (`a6bc064c02`, the original trust layer):** identity was `OriginKeys` when *every* origin URL normalized to `host/owner/repo`, otherwise it **flipped to the path key** — the doc comment said an unkeyable URL "flips the whole identity to path rather than being dropped from the key set… partial origin keys would fail open." So a `/srv/mirror.git` origin was trusted via `trusted_paths` ("this folder only"), and `trust_all` was never consulted against identity at all.
- **Aug 25 (`9669b4a85`, Codex's "finalize policy-driven activation"):** `ResolveTrustIdentity` now returns an *error* on any unnormalizable URL, `DecideEgress` maps that to `TrustReasonInvalidOrigin` and holds — **before** it ever looks at `trust_all`. `TestEgressDecision_UnparseableConfiguredOriginHolds` was added pinning exactly this, with `trust_all: true` in the fixture. The commit body ("preserve trust-gated checkpoint egress") gives no rationale for the change, and the doc was updated to describe the new behavior rather than justify it.

Net effect: a `ParseURL` that only understands `scheme://host/owner/repo` and `user@host:owner/repo` decides that a repo with a bare-path, `file://`, or single-segment origin (`git://localhost/foo.git`) can never sync — `entire trust`, `enable`-time recording, the push prompt's "Yes", **and** "Always/trust_all" all dead-end with "configured origin cannot be normalized."

## Yes — the sync-remote work is directly relevant

Consent and egress are keyed on two different remotes:

- **Trust identity** reads `origin`'s fetch + push URLs, hard-coded (`repopolicy.ResolveTrustIdentity`).
- **Where data actually goes** is the *elected* sync remote — `checkpoint_push_remote` → captured election → `origin` → sole remote → first remote (`strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote`), and the pre-push gate already has that remote in hand (`ps.remote`) when it calls `CheckpointEgressAllowed(ctx)`.

That mismatch produces three real cases:

| Setup | Today | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| `origin` = local bare mirror, `checkpoint_push_remote` (or captured) = GitHub | held forever, even with `trust_all` | the bug I hit; data would go to a normal GitHub remote |
| no `origin`, sole remote `upstream` = GitHub | path-keyed ("this folder only") | works, but consent doesn't name the destination and "all clones" scope is lost |
| `origin` = fork, sync remote = `upstream` | keyed on the fork | the prompt says "sync to your checkpoint sync remote" without saying which; a later election change (captured remote) doesn't re-ask |

## Options

1. **Minimal:** check `trust_all` before identity resolution, and restore the Aug 17 fallback (unkeyable origin → path identity) with an actionable `entire trust` message. Small, contained in `repopolicy/trust.go` + tests + doc. Fixes the dead end; leaves the origin/sync-remote mismatch as-is.
2. **Aligned (my recommendation):** key identity on the **elected sync remote's URLs** instead of `origin`, then fall back to path when they don't normalize; `trust_all` first. Consent then names the place transcripts actually go, and a changed election naturally re-asks (new destination, new consent — the Aug 17 comment's own principle). Cost: the election lives in `strategy`, which `settings` can't import, so it needs the same injection pattern `repopolicy.LocalSettingsTrusted` already uses, plus updating prompt copy ("all clones of X" → the sync remote), `status` trust line, and the doc.
3. Leave as designed, only fix the message.

Option 2 touches consent semantics, so it's your call rather than mine. Which way do you want to go?

Read all three; they're all merged and already in this branch. Here's what they say about this question.

## What the sync-remote trails establish

- **1046 (capture):** the motivating case is literally *"a fork with `origin` as an unpushable base repo"* — checkpoint data is *supposed* to go to a non-origin remote, elected from push behavior, announced on stderr, and `entire status` shows the destination. In `prePush` the elected remote (`ps.remote`) is resolved at line 76, **before** the trust gate at line 126 — the gate already uses it to count pending checkpoints, it just doesn't use it for identity.
- **1010 + 1015 (reads):** every read/discovery path was moved off hard-coded `origin` onto the elected remote, with `origin` demoted to a read-only legacy tier. The 1046 review even flagged the leftover origin-hardcodes as a bug and they were fixed.

So across the data plane, "origin" is no longer the repo's identity — the elected sync remote is. **Trust identity is the one remaining place still hard-coded to `origin`**, and it was written (Aug 17) before 1046 landed (Aug 18) and never reconciled.

## Why this matters more than a path-origin edge case

Your own still-open finding on 1046:

> *A stale `branch.<name>.remote` is a standing declaration, so one push can reroute sync off origin permanently… a `-u` push from months ago… first-capture-sticks makes the loss of origin sync permanent.*

Under global tracking today, that reroute is invisible to consent: the user trusted "all clones of `github.com/upstream/x`" (origin key), capture re-elects `fork`, and transcripts start flowing to `github.com/me/x-fork` with **no new consent** — the trust key never changes. If identity were keyed on the elected remote instead, a re-election flips the key, the gate holds, and the next push re-asks ("sync to `fork`?"). That turns the unresolved 1046 concern into a guarded path for every repo while the tier is on, and it's exactly the principle the Aug 17 code stated: *"any identity flip re-asks (new egress destination, new consent)."*

## Recommendation: key trust on the elected sync remote

Concretely:
1. `trust_all` checked first — unconditional consent needs no identity (fixes the dead end outright).
2. Identity = normalized fetch+push URLs of the **elected sync remote** (`checkpoint_push_remote` → captured → origin → sole → first; dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL when that mode is on). Unnormalizable → path key (restore the Aug 17 fallback), never a hard error.
3. Prompt/`trust`/`status` copy names the destination: "Yes — trust syncing this repo to `fork` (github.com/me/x-fork)".
4. Re-election under an active tier re-asks; pair it with 1046's existing "now syncing to …" announcement.

Cost: moderate, not trivial. `repopolicy` can't import `strategy` (cycle), so the remote has to come in via the same injection seam `LocalSettingsTrusted` uses or as a parameter from callers that already know it (`prePush`, `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs`, `trust`, `enable`, `status`). Files: `repopolicy/trust.go`, `hook_policy.go`, `trust_prompt.go`, `trust_cmd.go`, `setup.go` (enable), `status.go`, docs + tests. Roughly a focused half-day on top of what's already uncommitted.

Alternative if you'd rather not widen this PR: do (1) + the path fallback + a clear error now (small), and open a follow-up for (2)–(4) referencing your 1046 finding.

Which do you want — full alignment in this branch, or the small fix now and a follow-up?
so is the fix for a warning for elected remote then? adn this fixes the trust all?

Two different things — let me separate them:

**1. `trust_all` fix (small, independent).** Today `DecideEgress` resolves the origin identity *first* and fails closed if it can't, so `trust_all` never gets consulted for a repo with an unparseable origin. The fix is just ordering: if `trust_all` is on, allow — identity is irrelevant to "trust every repo". That alone fixes the "Always" answer and `trust_all: true` for local-path/`file://`/odd origins. Plus restoring the path-key fallback for the non-`trust_all` case so `entire trust` / `enable` / "Yes" work there too instead of erroring.

**2. Elected-remote fix (not a warning — a change of what consent is recorded against).** Today the trust *key* is origin's URL. The proposal is to make the key the **elected sync remote's** URL — the place transcripts actually go. Two consequences:
- `entire trust` / the "Yes" prompt record `github.com/me/x-fork` (the real destination) instead of `github.com/upstream/x` (the unpushable origin), and the copy says so.
- When capture re-elects a different remote, the key no longer matches → the gate **holds** and the next push **re-asks**. That hold + prompt is the user-visible part, so yes, it behaves like a warning at the moment of re-election — but the mechanism is the key change, not an extra message. A warning alone (keep origin key, print "now syncing to fork") would still let data flow to the new remote without consent.

So: #1 fixes `trust_all` by itself. #2 is about consent following the destination and is what closes the gap your 1046 finding exposed. They're separable — #1 can land now regardless of what we decide on #2.
if two repos push to two origins then whats the difference like why does this even matter if two differnet repos push to the same place either way

Fair pushback. For the common case it **doesn't** matter — one `origin`, pushes go to `origin`, both keys are the same URL, identical behavior. The key choice only shows up when the elected sync remote ≠ origin, and there are exactly three such situations:

**1. Two repos, two origins, same sync destination** (your example): repo1 `origin=A`, repo2 `origin=B`, both elected to push to `X`.
- Origin key: you're asked twice (trust A, trust B) even though transcripts from both go to the same place.
- Elected key: one answer (trust X) covers both.
Minor convenience either way; not a safety difference.

**2. Origin unpushable / unparseable, data goes elsewhere** (fork workflow, local bare mirror as origin, `checkpoint_push_remote` set): the origin key can be *unformable* — that's the dead end I hit — while the destination is a perfectly normal GitHub URL. Elected key just works. The small fix (`trust_all` first + path fallback) also unblocks this, less cleanly.

**3. Destination changes after consent** — the only case with a real safety angle. You trusted "all clones of `upstream/x`"; months later a stale `-u` declaration makes capture re-elect `fork`, and transcripts start going to a remote you never consented to sending them to. Origin key: nothing changes, nothing asks. Elected key: the key no longer matches → hold → re-ask. This is your open 1046 finding wearing its consent hat; the elected key is what makes it self-correcting.

So the honest summary: the *concept* isn't different ("may transcripts leave this machine"), the *key* only decides whether consent tracks the project or the destination, and that only bites in #3. If you don't consider silent re-election a real risk (or you'd rather fix it in 1046 by tightening capture itself), then #2 is over-engineering and the right move is just the small fix: `trust_all` checked first, path fallback instead of the hard error, clearer message. That's what I'd do now unless you want #3 closed on the consent side.

You're right — under `trust_all` there is no remote issue at all. Let me restate without the tangent:

**`trust_all` means "sync every repo, wherever it pushes."** Which remote, how many remotes, what the origin URL looks like — none of it should matter. The *only* bug is that today the code resolves the origin identity **before** it looks at `trust_all`, and if the origin URL isn't `host/owner/repo`-shaped (a local bare path, `file://`) that lookup errors and the repo is held anyway. So `trust_all` fails to do what it says for that one shape of origin. Fix: check `trust_all` first. One `if`, one test. Done.

**Everything I said about elected remotes only applies to per-repo trust** (people who answer "Yes, this repo" instead of "Always"), and even there it's a corner: which URL the per-repo entry is written under, and whether a later capture re-election should re-ask. That's a design question about the per-repo path, not about `trust_all`, and I over-weighted it. It doesn't need to be part of this PR.

So the concrete fix set for this branch:
1. `trust_all` before identity resolution.
2. For per-repo trust on an unparseable origin: fall back to the path key (the original Aug 17 behavior) instead of a hard error, so `entire trust` / `enable` / "Yes" work there too.
3. Keep the doc honest about both.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Real Claude Code end-to-end against the dev binary with global tracking on.
# Real HOME (real claude auth + real ~/.claude/settings.json user hooks, which
# call `entire` via PATH), sandboxed ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR so the real user settings
# file is untouched, dev binary first on PATH.
set -u
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
T="$S/real2"; rm -rf "$T"; mkdir -p "$T/config" "$T/bin" "$T/srv/acme"
ln -sf "$S/entire-bin" "$T/bin/entire"
export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH" ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$T/config" ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$T/gitconfig"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.name "Test User"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.email "test@example.com"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" commit.gpgsign false
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" init.defaultBranch main
echo '{"global":{"enabled":true}}' > "$T/config/settings.json"
echo "binary: $(command -v entire) ($(entire version 2>/dev/null | head -1))"

git daemon --reuseaddr --base-path="$T/srv" --export-all --enable=receive-pack --port=9419 --detach --pid-file="$T/daemon.pid"
sleep 1
trap 'kill $(cat "$T/daemon.pid") 2>/dev/null' EXIT

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  ✓ $1"; }
bad()  { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  ✗ $1"; }
check(){ if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1"; fi; }
section(){ echo; echo "=== $1"; }
claude_run() { # claude_run <outfile> <args...>
  local out="$1"; shift
  env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format json "$@" > "$out" 2> "$out.err" < /dev/null
  echo "    claude: rc=$? $(jq -r '"session=\(.session_id) cost=$\(.total_cost_usd) error=\(.is_error) → \(.result|.[:90])"' "$out" 2>/dev/null)"
  grep -v 'no stdin data' "$out.err" | sed 's/^/    claude stderr| /'
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- repo A
section "A1 fresh repo, git:// origin, first real Claude turn"
git init -q --bare "$T/srv/acme/widgets.git"
A="$T/repoA"; git init -q "$A"; cd "$A"
git remote add origin git://localhost:9419/acme/widgets.git
echo "# widgets" > README.md; git add README.md; git commit -q -m init; git push -q -u origin main
claude_run "$T/a1.json" "Create hello.py with a function greet(name) returning the string 'Hello, <name>!'. Do not run git commands."
SID=$(jq -r .session_id "$T/a1.json")
check "worktree clean except hello.py"     "test \"\$(git status --porcelain)\" = '?? hello.py'"
check "no .entire/ in worktree"            "! test -e .entire"
check "session state for $SID"             "test -f .git/entire-sessions/$SID.json"
check "shadow branch"                      "git branch --list 'entire/*' | grep -qv checkpoints"
check "git hooks installed"                "grep -q entire .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg"
LOG=$(ls .git/entire/worktree/*/logs/*.log | head -1)
check "no WARN/ERROR in hook log"          "! grep -qE '\"level\":\"(WARN|ERROR)\"|level=(WARN|ERROR)' $LOG"
grep -E '"level":"(WARN|ERROR)"' "$LOG" | cut -c1-260 | sed 's/^/    log| /'
entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "status header: Tracked globally"    "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '● Tracked globally'"
check "status --json enabled=true"         "entire status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -e '.enabled==true and .error==null'"

section "A2 second turn, same session (--resume)"
claude_run "$T/a2.json" --resume "$SID" "Now add a function shout(name) to hello.py that returns greet(name) upper-cased. Do not run git commands."
check "same session id"                    "test \"\$(jq -r .session_id $T/a2.json)\" = \"$SID\""
check "still no WARN/ERROR in hook log"    "! grep -qE '\"level\":\"(WARN|ERROR)\"' $LOG"
entire checkpoint list --pending 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    pending| /'

section "A3 commit → trailer + condensation"
git add hello.py; git commit -q -m "add greet/shout" 2>"$T/a3.err"; sed 's/^/    commit stderr| /' "$T/a3.err"
CP=$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)' | tr -d ' ')
check "Entire-Checkpoint trailer"          "test -n '$CP'"
check "v1 has exactly one checkpoint"      "test \$(git log --format=%s entire/checkpoints/v1 | grep -c '^Checkpoint:') -eq 1"
entire status 2>&1 | grep -E 'held|trusted' | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "status shows (1 held)"              "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '(1 held)'"

section "A4 push untrusted → hold; trust; push → drain"
git push origin main 2>"$T/a4.err"; sed 's/^/    push| /' "$T/a4.err"
check "hold message on stderr"             "grep -q 'checkpoint sync held' $T/a4.err"
check "no checkpoints on remote yet"       "! git ls-remote origin | grep -q entire/checkpoints"
entire trust 2>&1 | grep -v '^Warning: global' | sed 's/^/    trust| /'
check "trusted_origins has localhost/acme/widgets" "jq -e '.global.trusted_origins|index(\"localhost/acme/widgets\")' $T/config/settings.json"
echo "" >> README.md; git commit -q -am "tweak"; git push origin main 2>"$T/a4b.err"; sed 's/^/    push| /' "$T/a4b.err"
check "checkpoints on remote"              "git ls-remote origin | grep -q entire/checkpoints"
check "status trusted, no held"            "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'checkpoint sync: trusted' && ! entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q held"

section "A5 read back: checkpoint list / explain / session list / doctor"
entire checkpoint list 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    list| /'
entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint "$CP" --no-pager 2>&1 | sed -n '1,8p;/Transcript/,$p' | head -22 | sed 's/^/    explain| /'
check "explain shows both prompts"         "entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint $CP --no-pager 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'shout'"
entire session list 2>&1 | head -8 | sed 's/^/    sessions| /'
entire doctor 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    doctor| /'
check "doctor exits 0"                     "entire doctor >/dev/null 2>&1"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- repo B
section "B1 bare-path origin repo, real Claude turn, trust by path"
git init -q --bare "$T/mirror.git"
B="$T/repoB"; git init -q "$B"; cd "$B"
git remote add origin "$T/mirror.git"
echo "# b" > README.md; git add README.md; git commit -q -m init; git push -q -u origin main
claude_run "$T/b1.json" "Create notes.txt containing the single line 'hello from repo B'. Do not run git commands."
check "session captured"                   "ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json"
git add notes.txt; git commit -q -m "notes" 2>/dev/null
entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
git push origin main 2>"$T/b1.err"; sed 's/^/    push| /' "$T/b1.err"
check "held before trust"                  "grep -q 'checkpoint sync held' $T/b1.err"
entire trust 2>&1 | grep -v '^Warning: global' | sed 's/^/    trust| /'
check "trust by path succeeded"            "jq -e --arg p \"$B\" '.global.trusted_paths|index(\$p)' $T/config/settings.json"
echo "" >> README.md; git commit -q -am "tweak"; git push origin main 2>"$T/b2.err"; sed 's/^/    push| /' "$T/b2.err"
check "checkpoints reached the bare mirror" "git ls-remote origin | grep -q entire/checkpoints"

echo; echo "==================== $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ===================="
echo "test root: $T"
